title: 考研英语二2015年真题及答案解析（整卷）

sentences.text: A new study suggests that contrary to most surveys, people are actually more stressed at home than at work.
sentences.translation: 一项新研究表明,与大多数调查结果相反,人们实际上在家中比在工作时压力更大。研究人员测量了人们在工作时和在家时的皮质醇水平,这是一种压力标志物,结果发现在本应是避难所的地方,皮质醇水平反而更高。

sentences.text: Researchers measured people's cortisol, which is a stress marker, while they were at work and while they were at home and found it higher at what is supposed to be a place of refuge.
"Further contradicting conventional wisdom, we found that women as well as men have lower levels of stress at work than at home," writes one of the researchers, Sarah Damaske.
sentences.translation: 研究人员之一Sarah Damaske写道:"进一步违背传统观念的是,我们发现女性和男性一样,在工作时的压力水平低于在家时。"事实上,她指出,女性甚至表示在工作时感觉更好。"是男性而非女性,报告说在家比在工作时更快乐。"另一个令人惊讶的发现是,这些结果对有孩子和没有孩子的人都成立,但对没有孩子的人更为明显。这就是为什么在外工作的人拥有更好的健康状况。

sentences.text: In fact women even say they feel better at work, she notes.
"It is men, not women, who report being happier at home than at work."
Another surprise is that the findings hold true for both those with children and without, but more so for nonparents.
This is why people who work outside the home have better health.
What the study doesn't measure is whether people are still doing work when they're at home, whether it is household work or work brought home from the office.
sentences.translation: 懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2015-english-two/section2-part-a-1/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好blurring of roles, and the fact that the home front lags well behind the workplace in making adjustmentsfor working women, it's not surprising that women are more stressed at home.这项研究没有衡量的是,人们在家时是否仍在工作,无论是家务劳动还是从办公室带回家的工作。对许多男性来说,工作日结束是放松的时间。对于待在家里的女性,她们永远无法离开办公室。而对于在外工作的女性,她们常常在追赶家务任务。随着角色的模糊,以及家庭在为职业女性做出调整方面远远落后于职场这一事实,女性在家中压力更大就不足为奇了。

sentences.text: For many men, the end of the workday is a time to kick back.
For women who stay home, they never get to leave the office.
And for women who work outside the home, they often are playing catch-up with household tasks.

But it's not just a gender thing.
sentences.translation: 但这不仅仅是性别问题。在工作中,人们很清楚自己应该做什么:工作、赚钱、完成为了获得收入而必须做的任务。这种交换非常纯粹:员工投入体力或脑力劳动的时间,员工获得维持生活的报酬。

sentences.text: At work, people pretty much know what they're supposed to be doing: working, making money, doing the tasks they have to do in order to draw an income.
The bargain is very pure: Employee puts in hours of physical or mental labor and employee draws out life-sustaining moola.
So it's not surprising that people are more stressed at home.
sentences.translation: 因此,人们在家中压力更大并不令人惊讶。不仅任务显然无穷无尽,同事也更难激励。

sentences.text: Not only are the tasks apparently infinite, the co-workers are much harder to motivate.
Many first-generation students "struggle to navigate the middle-class culture of higher education, learn the 'rules of the game,' and take advantage of college resources," they write.
sentences.translation: 许多第一代大学生"难以适应高等教育的中产阶级文化,难以学会'游戏规则',难以利用大学资源",他们写道。当高校不谈论不同学生群体的阶层优势和劣势时,这就变成了一个更大的问题。"由于美国高校很少承认社会阶层如何影响学生的教育经历,许多第一代大学生对自己为何挣扎缺乏认识,也不理解'像他们一样'的学生如何才能进步。

sentences.text: And this becomes more of a problem when colleges don't talk about the class advantages and disadvantages of different groups of students.

"Because US colleges and universities seldom acknowledge how social class can affect students' educational experiences, many first-generation students lack insight about why they are struggling and do not understand how students 'like them' can improve."

Even in traditional offices, "the lingua franca of corporate America has gotten much more emotional and much more right-brained than it was 20 years ago," said Harvard Business School professor Nancy Koehn.
sentences.translation: 哈佛商学院教授Nancy Koehn说，即使在传统办公室里，"美国企业界的通用语言也比20年前变得更加感性化、更加偏重右脑思维"。她开始列举实例。"如果你我空降回1990年的财富500强公司，我们会发现像旅程、使命、激情这样的词汇使用频率要低得多。那时有目标、有战略、有目的，但我们不谈论能量，不谈论激情。"

sentences.text: She started spinning off examples.
"If you and I parachuted back to Fortune 500 companies in 1990, we would see much less frequent use of terms like journey, mission, passion.
There were goals, there were strategies, there were objectives, but we didn't talk about energy; we didn't talk about passion."
This new focus on personal fulfillment can help keep employees motivated amid increasingly loud debates over work-life balance.
sentences.translation: 这种对个人成就感的新关注可以帮助员工在关于工作生活平衡的日益激烈的辩论中保持动力。20世纪90年代的"妈妈之战"今天仍在继续,引发了关于为什么女性仍然无法兼顾一切的争论,以及像Sheryl Sandberg的《向前一步》这样的书籍,其标题本身就已成为一个流行语。像拔掉插头、离线、生活窍门、带宽和容量这样的术语都是关于在办公室和家庭之间设定界限。但如果你的工作是你的"激情所在",你就更有可能全身心投入其中,即使这意味着回家吃晚饭后在孩子们上床睡觉后还要长时间工作。

sentences.text: The "mommy wars" of the 1990s are still going on today, prompting arguments about why women still can't have it all and books like Sheryl Sandberg's Lean In, whose title has become a buzzword in its own right.
Terms like unplug, offline, life-hack, bandwidth, and capacity are all about setting boundaries between the office and the home.
But if your work is your "passion," you'll be more likely to devote yourself to it, even if that means going home for dinner and then working long after the kids are in bed.
Many people talked of the 288,000 new jobs the Labor Department reported for June, along with the drop in the unemployment rate to 6.1 percent, as good news.
sentences.translation: 许多人将劳工部报告的6月新增28.8万个就业岗位以及失业率降至6.1%视为好消息,他们是对的。目前看来,经济正在以适当的速度创造就业岗位。我们距离实现充分就业还有很长的路要走,但至少现在我们终于以更快的速度向前推进了。

sentences.text: And they were right.
For now it appears the economy is creating jobs at a decent pace.
We still have a long way to go to get back to full employment, but at least we are now finally moving forward at a faster pace.
Before explaining the connection to the Obamacare, it is worth making an important distinction.
sentences.translation: 在解释与Obamacare的联系之前,有必要做一个重要的区分。许多从事兼职工作的人实际上想要全职工作。他们从事兼职工作是因为这是他们能得到的全部。非自愿兼职工作的增加是劳动力市场疲软的证据,这意味着许多人将很难维持生计。懒笔记 · https://english-exam.lazynote.cn/kaoyan/sections/2015-english-two/section2-part-a-4/?f=p · 在线使⽤效果更好

sentences.text: Many people who work part-time jobs actually want full-time jobs.
They take part-time work because this is all they can get.
An increase in involuntary part-time work is evidence of weakness in the labor market and it means that many people will be having a very hard time making ends meet.
We know the difference between voluntary and involuntary part-time employment because people tell us.
sentences.translation: 我们知道自愿兼职和非自愿兼职就业之间的区别,因为人们告诉了我们。劳工部使用的调查询问人们在参照周内工作时间是否少于35小时。如果答案是肯定的,他们就被归类为兼职工作。然后调查询问他们在那一周工作时间少于35小时是因为想要少于全职工作还是因为别无选择。只有当他们告诉调查人员自己选择每周工作少于35小时时,才会被归类为自愿兼职工作者。

sentences.text: The survey used by the Labor Department asks people if they worked less than 35 hours in the reference week.
If the answer is "yes," they are classified as working part-time.
The survey then asks whether they worked less than 35 hours in that week because they wanted to work less than full time or because they had no choice.
They are only classified as voluntary part-time workers if they tell the survey taker they chose to work less than 35 hours a week.
The issue of voluntary part-time relates to Obamacare because one of the main purposes was to allow people to get insurance outside of employment.
sentences.translation: 自愿兼职问题与Obamacare相关,因为其主要目的之一是允许人们在就业之外获得保险。对许多人来说,尤其是那些有严重健康问题或家庭成员有严重健康问题的人,在Obamacare出台之前,获得保险的唯一途径是通过提供医疗保险的工作。

sentences.text: For many people, especially those with serious health conditions or family members with serious health conditions, before Obamacare the only way to get insurance was through a job that provided health insurance.
However, Obamacare has allowed more than 12 million people to either get insurance through Medicaid or the exchanges.
sentences.translation: 然而,Obamacare已使超过1200万人通过Medicaid或交易所获得保险。这些人以前可能觉得有必要找一份提供保险的全职工作,以便为自己和家人提供保障。有了Obamacare,就业和保险之间不再有关联。

sentences.text: These are people who may previously have felt the need to get a full-time job that provided insurance in order to cover themselves and their families.
With Obamacare there is no longer a link between employment and insurance.

sentences.text: It could be your commute to work, a trip into town or the way home.
Whichever it is, you know every twist and turn like the back of your hand.
On these sorts of trips it's easy to lose concentration on the driving and pay little attention to the passing scenery.
The consequence is that you perceive that the trip has taken less time than it actually has.
P2 This is the well-travelled road effect: People tend to underestimate the time it takes to travel a familiar route.
P3 The effect is caused by the way we allocate our attention.
When we travel down a well-known route, because we don't have to concentrate much, time seems to flow more quickly.
And afterwards, when we come to think back on it, we can't remember the journey well because we didn't pay much attention to it.
So we assume it was shorter.
